examples.en: My parents helped me in every way, with money and with heart.

examples.ko: 친구들이 물심양면 도와준 덕분에 무사히 이사했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my friends' all-out help, I moved safely.

examples.ko: 이 행사는 시민들의 물심양면 지원으로 열렸어요.
examples.en: This event was held with the citizens' full support.
The teacher does everything she can for her students.
Thank you so much for supporting me in every possible way.

examples.ko: 회사에서 물심양면 밀어준다고 해서 힘이 나요.
examples.en: The company says it will back me fully, so I feel encouraged.

explain: '물심양면으로'나 '물심양면 도와주다·지원하다·밀어주다'처럼 부사처럼 써요. 감사 인사나 칭찬할 때 자주 나오고, 보통 다른 사람을 돕는 일에 써요.
explain_en: It works like an adverb, as in '물심양면으로' or '물심양면 도와주다/지원하다/밀어주다'. It often appears in thank-you remarks and praise, and it is usually about helping other people.

en: pay for; make up for; compensate; recover

examples.ko: 친구 휴대폰을 떨어뜨려서 제가 물어내야 해요.
examples.en: I dropped my friend's phone, so I have to pay for it.
The child who broke the window paid for it.

examples.ko: 빌린 책을 잃어버리면 새 책으로 물어내요.
examples.en: If you lose a borrowed book, you replace it with a new one.
I scratched the rental car, and they told me to pay for the repairs.
I'll make up for what I broke myself.
If you don't want to pay for damage, be careful from the start.

explain: '갚다'는 빌린 것을 돌려줄 때 쓰고, '물어내다'는 내가 망가뜨리거나 손해를 입힌 것의 값을 내놓을 때 써요. 딱딱하게는 '변상하다'라고도 하지만 말할 때는 '물어내다'를 많이 써요. 보통 '~을/를 물어내다' 형태예요.
explain_en: '갚다' is for returning something you borrowed, while '물어내다' is for paying for something you broke or a loss you caused. A formal word is '변상하다', but in speech '물어내다' is common. It is usually used as '~을/를 물어내다'.

en: come into one's prime; hit one's stride

examples.ko: 요즘 그 배우의 연기가 한창 물올랐어요.
examples.en: That actor's acting is at its peak these days.
When spring comes, sap rises in every branch.
With his peak skills, he won the competition.
As the weather warms up, the willow trees start to come alive too.

examples.ko: 한창 물오른 선수라서 다음 경기도 기대돼요.
examples.en: He is a player in top form, so I'm looking forward to the next game too.

examples.ko: 요즘 글솜씨가 물올라서 글이 잘 써져요.
examples.en: My writing has hit its stride lately, so the words come easily.

explain: 나무에 물이 올라 싱싱해지는 모습에서, 사람의 연기·실력·인기가 한창 좋아질 때도 써요. '물오른 연기', '물오른 실력'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '오르다'가 르 불규칙이라 '물올라요, 물올랐어요'로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It describes a tree getting fresh as sap rises, and it is also used when a person's acting, skill or popularity is at its best. It often appears as '물오른 연기' or '물오른 실력'. Because '오르다' is a 르-irregular verb, it becomes '물올라요' and '물올랐어요'.

examples.en: The kids are splashing around happily in the valley stream.
I only splashed around in the shallow part of the pool.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 여름마다 시냇가에서 물장구를 치며 놀았어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I played splashing around in the creek every summer.

examples.ko: 발로 물장구를 치면 물이 사방으로 튀어요.
examples.en: If you kick and splash with your feet, water flies everywhere.

examples.ko: 동생은 수영은 못 하고 물장구만 좋아해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling can't swim and only likes splashing about.

examples.ko: 물장구 소리가 들려서 가 봤더니 아이들이 있었어요.
examples.en: I heard splashing, so I went to look, and there were kids.

explain: 보통 '물장구를 치다'로 써요. 수영할 때 발차기와 달리 물에서 발이나 손으로 물을 치며 노는 모습에 어울려요. 주로 아이들이 노는 장면에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '물장구를 치다'. Unlike a swimming kick, it suits playful splashing in water with your feet or hands. It mostly appears in scenes of children playing.

examples.ko: 폭우로 인명 피해는 없었지만 물적 피해는 컸어요.
examples.en: There were no casualties from the heavy rain, but the property damage was big.
The police are looking for physical evidence.

examples.ko: 회사가 어려워서 인적, 물적 자원이 많이 부족해요.
examples.en: The company is struggling, so human and material resources are very short.

examples.ko: 이 사고로 물적 손해가 얼마나 났는지 조사해요.
examples.en: They are investigating how much material loss this accident caused.
To start a business, you also need a material base.

examples.ko: 정부가 피해 지역에 물적 지원을 약속했어요.
examples.en: The government promised material support for the affected area.

explain: 관형사라서 뒤에 꼭 명사가 와요. 물적 피해, 물적 증거, 물적 자원처럼 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '인적'이고, 뉴스의 사고 보도에서 '인적·물적 피해'로 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a determiner, so a noun must follow, as in 물적 피해, 물적 증거 and 물적 자원. Its counterpart is '인적', and the two often appear together as '인적·물적 피해' in accident news.

en: the ways of the world; how things are

examples.ko: 외국에서 오래 살아서 한국 물정을 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: I lived abroad for a long time, so I don't know how things work in Korea.
He's still young and doesn't know how the world works.

examples.ko: 이 동네 물정에 밝은 사람이 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish there were someone who knows this neighborhood well.

examples.ko: 그는 물정 모르고 비싼 값에 샀어요.
examples.en: He didn't know the going prices and bought it at a high price.
I'm naive about the world, so I was easily fooled.

examples.ko: 유학 다녀오니 요즘 물정이 많이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: After studying abroad, I found how things are now has changed a lot.

explain: 거의 '세상 물정', '이곳 물정'처럼 쓰고, '밝다·어둡다·모르다'와 자주 함께 나와요. 어른이 어린 사람이나 순진한 사람에게 '물정을 모른다'고 하면 약간 핀잔하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in forms like '세상 물정' or '이곳 물정', often with '밝다', '어둡다' or '모르다'. When an adult says someone '물정을 모른다', it can sound a little like a scolding.

examples.ko: 영화를 만들려면 먼저 물주를 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: To make a movie, you first have to find a backer.

examples.ko: 그 사업의 물주가 누구인지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows who is bankrolling that business.
My older brother is paying today, so order whatever you like.

examples.ko: 물주가 갑자기 손을 떼서 공사가 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The financier suddenly pulled out, so construction stopped.

examples.ko: 좋은 물주를 만나서 가게를 열 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I met a good backer and was able to open a shop.

examples.ko: 친구가 물주 노릇을 하면서 밥을 샀어요.
examples.en: My friend played the role of the one paying and bought us a meal.

explain: '투자자'보다 가볍고 입말에 가까운 말이에요. 친구 사이에서는 오늘 돈을 내는 사람을 농담으로 '물주'라고도 해요. '물주를 찾다', '물주 노릇'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is lighter and more colloquial than '투자자' (investor). Among friends, the person paying today is jokingly called the '물주'. It appears in forms like '물주를 찾다' and '물주 노릇'.

examples.en: I have a suspicion, but no hard evidence.
The police found physical evidence to prove the crime.

examples.ko: 확실한 물증이 나와서 그는 결국 인정했어요.
examples.en: Solid evidence came out, so he finally admitted it.

examples.ko: 말만 하지 말고 물증을 보여 주세요.
examples.en: Don't just talk; show me the proof.
The photo became the most important piece of evidence.

examples.ko: 물증 없이 의심만 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't just suspect people without any proof.

explain: '심증'과 짝으로 외워 두면 좋아요. 심증은 마음속으로 하는 짐작이고, 물증은 눈에 보이는 물건이나 자료예요. '증거'보다 사진·문서·물건처럼 실제로 남아 있는 것을 말하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is useful to learn it as a pair with '심증'. '심증' is a conviction in your mind, while '물증' is something visible like an object or document. Compared with '증거', it feels more like something real that remains, such as a photo, document or item.

examples.ko: 물질주의에 빠지면 돈으로 행복을 재기 쉬워요.
examples.en: When you fall into materialism, it's easy to measure happiness by money.

examples.ko: 요즘 사회는 물질주의가 너무 심하다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think society these days is too materialistic.
He wrote a book criticizing materialism.
I want to break free from materialistic thinking.

examples.ko: 젊은 세대의 물질주의가 문제라는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article saying the materialism of the young generation is a problem.
My grandfather told me to be wary of materialism.

explain: 돈과 물건을 가장 중요하게 여기는 태도를 비판하거나 걱정할 때 주로 써요. 사람에게는 '물질주의적이다'라고 하고, 글이나 토론, 칼럼에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is mostly used to criticize or worry about an attitude that puts money and things first. For a person you say '물질주의적이다', and the word often appears in essays, discussions and columns.

examples.en: The mushy, bursting feeling was strange.
When I pressed it with my hand, it sank in squishily.
I don't like the mushy texture when I chew it.

examples.ko: 진흙 위를 걷자 발밑이 물컹물컹 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: When I walked on the mud, the ground felt squishy under my feet.
I overcooked it, so it turned mushy and fell apart.
I kneaded the soft, squishy dough with my hands.

explain: 손으로 누르거나 입에서 씹을 때 무르고 눌리는 느낌이 계속될 때 써요. '물컹물컹 씹히다', '물컹물컹 눌리다'처럼 동사 앞에 오고, '물컹물컹한'처럼 꾸며 줄 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when something feels soft and squishy over and over as you press it or chew it. It comes before verbs, as in '물컹물컹 씹히다' and '물컹물컹 눌리다', and can also modify a noun as '물컹물컹한'.

examples.en: The persimmon is so ripe that it's mushy.
The banana is mushy, so I don't want to eat it.

examples.ko: 발밑에서 물컹한 느낌이 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I felt something squishy under my foot and was startled.
If you overcook eggplant, the texture turns mushy.
Please cook it just lightly so it doesn't get mushy.
The tofu I froze and thawed was mushy.

explain: 푹 익은 과일이나 삶은 채소처럼 눌러 보면 속이 무르게 들어가는 느낌이에요. 부드러운 것과 달리 식감이 별로라는 말투로 쓸 때가 많아요. '말랑하다'는 귀엽고 부드러운 느낌이라 쓰임이 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It describes the feeling of overripe fruit or boiled vegetables, where the inside gives way when pressed. Unlike simply 'soft', it is often said with a sense that the texture is unpleasant. '말랑하다' feels cute and soft, so its use is a bit different.

examples.ko: 인터넷에서 그 가수가 뭇매를 맞고 있어요.
examples.en: That singer is getting hammered with criticism online.

examples.ko: 잘못된 발언으로 정치인이 여론의 뭇매를 맞았어요.
examples.en: The politician was lashed by public opinion over his wrong remarks.

examples.ko: 광고가 논란이 되어 회사가 뭇매를 맞았어요.
examples.en: The ad caused controversy, and the company took a lot of heat.
I apologized honestly, ready to take the heat.

examples.ko: 그 발표는 비판의 뭇매를 피하지 못했어요.
examples.en: That announcement couldn't avoid a barrage of criticism.
Under the pile-on from people, he finally apologized.

explain: 거의 '뭇매를 맞다' 형태로 써요. 원래는 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 때리는 매를 뜻하고, 뉴스에서는 '여론의 뭇매'처럼 비판이 한꺼번에 쏟아지는 상황에 비유해서 써요.

phrases.example: 광고 논란으로 그 회사가 뭇매를 맞았어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람에게 한꺼번에 심한 비난을 받을 때 써요. 뉴스나 인터넷 기사에 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many people criticize someone harshly at once; common in news and online articles.

explain_en: It is almost always used as '뭇매를 맞다'. Originally it means a beating from many people at once, and in the news it is used figuratively, as in '여론의 뭇매', for criticism pouring in all at once.

examples.ko: 가방 속에서 빵이 눌려서 뭉개진 채로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The bread got pressed in my bag and came out squashed.
It rained, and my makeup got completely smudged.
If you enlarge the photo a lot, the letters get blurry.

examples.ko: 딸기가 뭉개지지 않게 조심히 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please carry the strawberries carefully so they don't get squashed.
The cake lost its shape, so I made it again.

examples.ko: 발에 밟힌 꽃이 땅에 뭉개져 있어요.
examples.en: The flower stepped on is squashed on the ground.

explain: 눌리거나 밟혀서 모양이 망가질 때 써요. 화장이 번지거나 사진·글씨가 흐릿해질 때도 쓸 수 있어요. 능동형 '뭉개다'는 '일을 미적거리다'라는 뜻으로도 써서, 이 단어와 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요.
explain_en: It is used when something loses its shape by being pressed or stepped on. It can also be used when makeup smudges or when a photo or text becomes blurry. The active form '뭉개다' is also used to mean putting off a task, so be careful not to confuse the two.

examples.en: White clouds billowed up in the sky.
Smoke is rising in billows from the chimney.

examples.ko: 뭉게뭉게 떠 있는 구름을 보며 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I lay there watching the puffy clouds floating by.
I made a soup with steam billowing off it.
Clouds gather in puffs in the autumn sky.
I can see smoke pouring out of the factory in billows.

explain: 구름, 연기, 김이 둥글고 크게 계속 피어오르는 모습에 써요. '피어오르다, 올라가다, 나다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 같은 뿌리의 '뭉게구름'은 뭉게뭉게 떠 있는 구름이에요.
explain_en: It describes clouds, smoke or steam rising in big round puffs, one after another. It goes well with verbs like '피어오르다', '올라가다' and '나다'. The related word '뭉게구름' is a puffy cloud.

examples.en: On Sunday mornings I just lounge around in bed.
Stop dawdling and get ready quickly.
I kept dawdling without doing my homework.

examples.ko: 왜 아직도 문 앞에서 뭉그적거리고 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you still hanging around at the door?
Every morning I dawdle in my room and end up late.

examples.ko: 동생이 이불 속에서 뭉그적거려서 같이 못 나갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling kept lingering under the blanket, so we couldn't leave together.

explain: 해야 할 일이 있는데 일어나거나 움직이지 않고 미적거릴 때 써요. '꾸물거리다'와 비슷하지만 제자리에서 몸을 움직이지 않고 미루는 장면에 잘 어울려요. 약간 게으르다고 나무라는 말투로도 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when you have something to do but linger without getting up or moving. It is similar to '꾸물거리다' but fits scenes where someone stays in place and puts things off. It can also carry a mild tone of scolding someone for being lazy.

examples.en: Please simmer it gently until the broth gets rich.

examples.ko: 약한 불에서 뭉근히 졸이면 맛이 깊어져요.
examples.en: If you reduce it slowly over low heat, the flavor gets deeper.
I boiled the meat slowly, and it's very tender.
Red bean porridge tastes good when you stir it slowly for a long time.

examples.ko: 찌개가 뭉근히 끓는 동안 밥을 지었어요.
examples.en: I cooked rice while the stew simmered gently.
I slow-simmered ox bones to make seolleongtang.

explain: 센 불이 아니라 약한 불에서 오래 천천히 조리할 때 써요. '끓이다, 졸이다, 고다, 삶다'와 잘 어울리고 요리법 글에서 자주 나와요. '푹'은 충분히 오래 익힌다는 느낌이라 불 세기와는 상관없어요.
explain_en: It is used when cooking slowly over low heat rather than high heat. It pairs well with '끓이다', '졸이다', '고다' and '삶다', and often appears in recipes. '푹' means cooking thoroughly for a long time and says nothing about the heat level.

examples.en: I lumped the various opinions into one and presented them.

examples.ko: 문제를 뭉뚱그려 말하지 말고 하나씩 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't talk about the problems all at once; explain them one by one.
It's easier if you group similar items together.

examples.ko: 그 사람들을 다 뭉뚱그려서 욕하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't lump all those people together and curse them.

examples.ko: 사건의 원인을 뭉뚱그리지 말고 자세히 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't gloss over the cause of the incident; tell me in detail.
We glossed over the details and moved on.

explain: 여러 가지를 따로 나누지 않고 크게 하나로 묶거나 대충 뭉쳐서 말할 때 써요. '요약하다'는 핵심을 간추리는 것이고, '뭉뚱그리다'는 세부를 구분하지 않고 대충 묶는 느낌이 있어요. 그래서 '뭉뚱그려 말하다'는 자세히 말하지 않는다는 뜻으로도 들려요.
explain_en: It is used when you bundle many things together without separating them, or talk about them roughly. '요약하다' means picking out the key points, while '뭉뚱그리다' feels like grouping things loosely without distinguishing details. So '뭉뚱그려 말하다' can also sound like not going into detail.

en: large sum of money; wad of cash

examples.en: A huge sum of money left the bank all at once.
He carried a wad of cash around in his bag.
A big chunk of money came in as a year-end bonus.
Large sums of money are flowing into the real estate market.

examples.ko: 갑자기 뭉칫돈이 생기면 어디에 쓸 거예요?
examples.en: If you suddenly got a big pile of money, what would you spend it on?

examples.ko: 계좌에 뭉칫돈이 들어온 이유를 설명해야 했어요.
examples.en: I had to explain why a large sum came into my account.

explain: 한꺼번에 큰돈이 오가거나 한 덩어리로 있는 돈을 말해요. 뉴스에서 '뭉칫돈이 몰리다', '뭉칫돈이 빠져나가다'처럼 자주 나와요. '목돈'과 비슷하지만 뭉칫돈은 한꺼번에 움직이는 큰돈이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It refers to a large sum of money moving all at once or sitting as one lump. In the news it often appears as '뭉칫돈이 몰리다' or '뭉칫돈이 빠져나가다'. It is similar to '목돈', but '뭉칫돈' has a stronger feel of big money moving in one go.

examples.en: My hair has been falling out in clumps lately, and I'm worried.
The hairdresser chopped off a big chunk of my hair.
I tore off a big chunk of the cake by hand and ate it.
A big chunk of this month's pay went out all at once.
A big chunk in the middle of the book was torn out.

examples.ko: 기억이 뭉텅 사라진 것처럼 하나도 생각 안 나요.
examples.en: It's as if a big chunk of my memory vanished; I can't recall any of it.

explain: 한 덩어리를 크게 잘라 내거나 한꺼번에 빠지고 없어질 때 써요. 머리카락, 돈, 기억처럼 한번에 많은 양이 사라지는 장면에 어울려요. '뭉텅뭉텅'처럼 반복해서도 쓰고, '뭉텅이'와 같은 뿌리의 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used when a big lump is cut off or a large amount drops or disappears at once. It suits scenes where much is lost in one go, like hair, money or memory. It can also be repeated as '뭉텅뭉텅', and it comes from the same root as '뭉텅이'.

examples.en: A whole clump of my hair fell out.
A wad of receipts came out of the drawer.
She tore off the bread in big chunks and gave it to me.
I swept up the fallen leaves one big pile at a time.
I went to the store holding a wad of cash.
I put the laundry into the washing machine in one big lump.

explain: 한데 뭉쳐 있는 덩어리를 가리키고 '한 뭉텅이'처럼 양을 셀 때도 써요. '덩어리'보다 입말에 가깝고, 꽤 많은 양이 한꺼번에 뭉쳐 있다는 느낌이 있어요. '뭉텅이로', '뭉텅이째'처럼 조사나 접미사와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It points to a clump of things stuck together, and is also used to count amounts as in '한 뭉텅이'. It is more colloquial than '덩어리' and suggests a fairly large amount bunched together. It often appears with particles or suffixes, as in '뭉텅이로' and '뭉텅이째'.

examples.ko: 연필 끝이 뭉툭해서 잘 안 써져요.
examples.en: The pencil tip is blunt, so it doesn't write well.
My fingertips are stubby and short.

examples.ko: 뭉툭한 칼로는 야채가 잘 안 썰려요.
examples.en: Vegetables don't cut well with a dull knife.
I often hear that the tip of my nose is rounded.
If the toe of the shoe is rounded, your feet are comfortable.
Scissors for kids are made with blunt tips.

explain: 끝이 뾰족하지 않고 두툼하고 무딘 모양을 말해요. 반대말은 '뾰족하다'나 '날카롭다'예요. '무디다'는 날이 잘 안 드는 것에 쓰고, '뭉툭하다'는 끝의 생김새에 쓴다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes a shape whose end is thick and blunt rather than pointed. Its opposites are '뾰족하다' and '날카롭다'. '무디다' is for things whose edge doesn't cut well, while '뭉툭하다' is about the shape of the tip.

examples.en: This area is still undeveloped.
It's undeveloped land, so the land price is cheap.
I heard a new road will be built in the undeveloped area.
Half of the island remains undeveloped.
They're trying to find untapped resources and develop them.

examples.ko: 그 지역은 미개발이라 자연이 잘 보존돼 있어요.
examples.en: That area is undeveloped, so nature is well preserved.

explain: '미개발 지역', '미개발 토지', '미개발 자원'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사 앞에 붙여 많이 써요. '미-'는 '아직 ~하지 않은'이라는 뜻이라 '미완성', '미확인'과 같은 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. 반대는 '개발'이나 '개발된'이에요.
explain_en: It is often placed before a noun, as in '미개발 지역', '미개발 토지' and '미개발 자원'. The prefix '미-' means 'not yet ~', so it is easy to remember with words like '미완성' and '미확인'. The opposite is '개발' or '개발된'.
